newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Greece deports hundreds of Albanians-police.
newsitem.headline: Greece deports hundreds of Albanians-police.

text.p: Hundreds of Albanians have been deported from Greece in a crackdown on illegal immigration, Albanian police said on Thursday.

The deportation drive on Wednesday night followed the arrest of a number of immigrants earlier in the week in connection with a series of burglaries in an Athens suburb, believed to be the work of an Albanian crime ring.

Police at the Kakavie border crossing in southern Albania, 250 km (155 miles) south of Tirana, said around 10 buses brought back 300 Albanians -- three times the number Albania expects in regular deportations.

"There usually come two to three buses on Tuesdays and Fridays, but last night there were eight to 10 buses coming mainly from Athens -- unlike other times when they come from other Greek cities," a policeman said.
"That might be a start of a new deportation wave."

Greece deported thousands of Albanians in 1994 when relations hit a low. The issues of illegal Albanian workers in Greece and the rights of an ethnic Greek minority in southern Albania sparking serious disputes between the two countries.

After four years of tension Tirana and Athens settled most of their grievances, signing a friendship treaty and an accord to legalise the status of Albanian immigrants in Greece in March and May of last year.
Athens agreed to legalise the status of Albanian immigrants in Greece, estimated at 350,000, but the law has yet to be passed.
